THE ONLY DELTA at (d)/S2: the leg-cap normalization - knee |tau[4]|/9.576795, mp |tau[6]|/1.657925, ankle SIGN-GATED (tau[5] < 0 at the measured plantar cap 6.247077; tau[5] >= 0 at the measured dorsal cap 1.251106), hip |tau[3]|/CAP['hip'] held. pre_registration.verdict_law: wall(set, trajectory) := max over the 21 nodes of max(stance_ratio, posture_ratio). achievable_wall(D) := the minimum wall over this lane's (d) runs (three starts, per-start results all reported). REOPENS iff achievable_wall(D) < 1.0; CLOSED iff >= 1.0. The maximin bound LB := max over nodes of (min over theta in [-0.6, 0.6] of the stance_ratio at that node) is a THEOREM-grade lower bound on achievable_wall(D) within the formulation: the wall at any node >= that node's stance_ratio >= the node's theta-minimum, and theta is decoupled across nodes in the leg columns; LB > 1.0 therefore closes the question REGARDLESS of what the optimizer finds, and every optimizer run must return wall >= LB (its own falsifier)

findings: F1 - THE RE-HEARING ANSWER: the (d) re-block is a property of the ENVELOPE. Three independent starts of the wave-10 collocation at the measured caps converge to walls 1.1558-1.1571 (the banked optimum's own re-price is 1.157587 - the optimizer improves it by at most 0.0018), every one ankle-bound, and the maximin bound proves nothing in the formulation can beat 1.0425: the statics receipt's F6 open door ('a re-collocation at the measured caps could redistribute the ankle load') is measured SHUT at S1. The banked wave-10 optimum was never the problem - the measured ankle cap is.

F2 - WHERE THE LOAD CAN AND CANNOT SHIFT: the histogram's room is real - the probe shows theta moves CAN unload the ankle into hip+knee node-wise (at phi 0.5 the ankle ratio falls 1.1535 -> 0.9416 as theta goes +0.6 -> -0.1 while the hip rises to 1.107) - but the shift saturates the HIP at phis 0.30-0.45 before the ankle clears 1.0 (the bound's over-unity set), and the mission's own objective (the wave-10 mean-of-maxima) does not drive the trajectory to the node-wise optimum. The knee's measured headroom (cap x1.443 of doc) is never the binding constraint: the hip, UNCHANGED from doc, is what blocks the shift. The borrowed hip/posture cap (CAP_POST = CAP['hip'] = 11.21825 at the instrument, held) now owns the next question the way the ankle owned the last one.

F3 - THE QUADRUPED LINE STANDS ALONE: the vendored statics module's own verdict rule ('if no theta at some stance node brings every demand/cap ratio under 1.0, the bipedal hindlimb lift is STATICALLY INFEASIBLE at any trunk pitch -- the quadruped lane is confirmed') is measured TRUE at the measured (d) caps at phis 0.30-0.45. At the trajectory level as at the statics level, the measured-caps bipedal vault is closed at S1; the quadruped gait line is the only admissible line at these caps.

F4 - THE S2 BRACKET: at the SI-matched scale the collocation walls are 9.64-9.66 (bound 8.435635), matching the statics receipt's S2 re-price 9.666383 - the walker can neither hold nor vault; the scale gate stands on every verdict.

F5 - INSTRUMENT NOTE: the wave-10 optimum reproduces BYTE-EXACT on this clone (numpy 2.2.6 / scipy 1.17.0) - the banked SLSQP artifact is bit-stable across the lineage's machines and years, which upgrades every downstream band that assumed cross-machine float noise.
